morphology_as_written: dropwise addition of a copper ethanolic solution into an aqueous solution of the deprotonated ligand, affording cuboctahedral crystals
notes: Ligand deprotonated with NaHCO3 in water first, copper in ethanol added dropwise. metal_conc_mM computed over 190 mL. Yield 89.6%. BET 1410 m2/g. CO2 7.92 mmol/g at 196 K, 1 bar.

morphology_as_written: long crystals were obtained for the SWCNT@HKUST-1 composite, a nontypical HKUST-1 crystal habit which hint a templated growth
mechanism_as_written: HKUST-1 nucleates heterogeneously on the functional groups of the nanotubes and grows along them.
notes: Composite, not pure HKUST-1. BET 1714 m2/g; CO2 8.75 mmol/g at 196 K, 1 bar.

morphology_as_written: the morphology was more uniform and bipyramid-like ... average crystal diameters were about ... 55 um (n-HKUST-1)
notes: 9 mmol Cu salt in 30 mL water + 5 mmol H3BTC in 30 mL ethanol; 15 min ultrasound at 25 C to nucleate, then static 110 C 24 h; DMF-free. A square bipyramid is an octahedron; the authors write 'bipyramid-like'. BET 1153 m2/g. The same authors' earlier mixing procedure gave irregular crystals of about 10 um (their Table 4).

morphology_as_written: samples obtained from copper(II) sulfate ... the morphology was more uniform and bipyramid-like ... about 16 um (s-HKUST-1)
notes: The paper's Table 4 lists this sample as 'Irregular, ~10,000 nm', which contradicts the SEM text; the text is entered. BET 937 m2/g. Copper(II) chloride under the same conditions gave no product.

morphology_as_written: the surface of HKUST-1 obtained from copper(II) acetate displays a board-like morphology of various sizes
mechanism_as_written: Acetate ions compete with BTC3- during crystallisation and may be partly incorporated.
notes: Table 4 calls the same sample 'rod-like'. Yield 96% (highest of the salts) but BET only 553 m2/g.
Secondary: taken from the literature comparison table of klemba2025 (Materials 2025, 18, 676), which cites Ricco et al. 2018. BET 10-130 m2/g, lower for longer time.
Secondary, as ricco2018-1. BET 900-1600 m2/g, highest at 3 h.

morphology_as_written: composed of tetrahedral crystals with average diameters of approximately 5-15 um
varied: solvent (EtOH-H2O vs DMF-H2O) and heating (oven vs microwave)
notes: Sample HKUST-1solv.1. 8.58 mmol Cu, 0.525 g H3BTC (2.50 mmol); metal_conc_mM computed over 35 mL. Entered as 'other' because a tetrahedron is forbidden by the Fm-3m symmetry of HKUST-1; klemba2025 summarises the same images as 'bipyramid'. BET 1648 m2/g.

morphology_as_written: crystals with the sizes in the range ~5-20 um, so the solvent system does not impact remarkably on size and morphology
varied: solvent (EtOH-H2O vs DMF-H2O) and heating (oven vs microwave)
notes: Sample HKUST-1solv.2. The authors' statement is that EtOH-H2O and DMF-H2O give the same habit and similar size.

solvent: H2O/DMF (20 mL DMF; water volume not stated)
morphology_as_written: larger crystals with the almost ideal tetrahedral shape and sizes of around 25-40 um ... more homogeneous distribution of crystals in size and shape
varied: solvent (EtOH-H2O vs DMF-H2O) and heating (oven vs microwave)
mechanism_as_written: Under microwave heating, crystal growth probably outpaces nucleation, so crystals are larger and more uniform.
notes: Sample HKUST-1mw, 200 W, 30 min. Cu 8.58 mmol, H3BTC 4.76 mmol. Weak extra peaks index in Pm-3m. BET 1617 m2/g. Shape word 'tetrahedral' handled as in isaeva2020-1.

morphology_as_written: the mechanically untreated materials have the shape of octahedra ... The crystal size of HKUST-1 ranges from a few micrometers to up to 30 um
size_basis: size range ('a few micrometers to up to 30 um')
notes: Heated at 0.5 C/min to 85 C, held 12 h, cooled at 1 C/min. The lower bound of size_um is the curator's reading of 'a few micrometers'. Hand grinding deforms the octahedra (to <= 10 um); ball milling destroys the shape. CO2 uptakes for all three are in co2_adsorption.csv. Another additive-free octahedron benchmark.

morphology_as_written: a typical single-crystal morphology exhibiting octahedral crystals with slightly circular edges
varied: metal substitution (10% Ni, Co, Rh) and benzoic acid
notes: Sample BH-Cu100. Stirred 2 h at room temperature, then 24 h at 393 K. BET 1654 m2/g, CO2 2.8 mmol/g at 298 K.

metal_salt: Cu(NO3)2·2.5H2O with 10 mol% Ni, Co or Rh salt
additive: 10 mol% of the Cu replaced by Ni(NO3)2, Co(NO3)2 or Rh2(OAc)4
morphology_as_written: the ion substitution in the structure favoring the formation of truncated octahedra particles
varied: metal substitution (10% Ni, Co, Rh) and benzoic acid
notes: Mixed-metal HKUST-1; 7.4-8.4 mol% of Cu actually substituted (EDS). One record for the three metals because the text describes them together.

morphology_as_written: maintains the overall morphology of the parent HKUST-1. Still, the surfaces are now rugged, featuring irregular needle-like pores ... particle size ... approximately 1.5 times larger
varied: metal substitution (10% Ni, Co, Rh) and benzoic acid
mechanism_as_written: Benzoic acid replaces part of the BTC linker and creates defects that give hierarchical porosity.
notes: Sample HH-Cu100. The recipe lists 2.06 mmol Cu plus 0.22 mmol of a second metal salt for the mixed-metal versions; for HH-Cu100 the total metal used is not stated separately, so metal_conc_mM and linker_to_metal are computed from 2.28 mmol total metal and 1.9 mmol H3BTC. BET 1666 m2/g, CO2 1.0 mmol/g at 298 K.
